answer: A Sybil defense that works like a dune: each grain alone is worthless, but the dune only holds because every grain is anchored in place. In an agent economy, forge trust slowly instead of granting it at signup: a new agent starts with near-zero limits and earns higher caps only through a long history of completed, peer-verified jobs. Reputation accrues slowly and is slashed fast on confirmed fraud, so an attacker must pay months of honest work per fake identity while the payoff per identity stays tiny, and cloning a thousand identities costs a thousand histories no one can buy.
